content.title: IF YOU ATE THIS EVERY DAY FOR {{30 DAYS}}, YOUR BODY WOULD CHANGE LIKE THIS
facts: If you ate **beets** every day for 2 weeks, your stamina during workouts would noticeably improve as nitrates widen your blood vessels and your muscles get more oxygen per breath.
If you ate **oats** every day for 30 days, your cholesterol numbers would likely drop as the beta-glucan fiber grabs onto bile acids and drags them out of your body.
If you ate **fermented yogurt** every day for 3 weeks, your bloating would ease as live cultures crowd out gas-producing bacteria in your gut.
If you ate **pumpkin seeds** every day for 2 weeks, you'd likely fall asleep faster thanks to their natural tryptophan and magnesium working together at night.
If you ate **blueberries** every day for 1 month, your memory recall would sharpen as their antioxidants reduce inflammation around brain cells.
If you ate **sardines** every day for 2 weeks, your joint stiffness would fade as the omega-3s calm down inflammatory compounds in your blood.
If you ate **lentils** every day for 10 days, your blood sugar swings would smooth out as the slow-digesting fiber and protein blunt glucose spikes.
If you ate **sauerkraut** every day for 3 weeks, your skin breakouts could clear up as gut bacteria shift and reduce overall body inflammation.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
A few of these deserve a second look. Beets are loaded with natural nitrates that your body converts into nitric oxide, which relaxes blood vessel walls so oxygen-rich blood reaches working muscles faster — that's why endurance athletes swear by beet juice before a race. Oats work differently: their beta-glucan fiber forms a gel in your gut that binds to cholesterol-carrying bile acids, forcing your liver to pull more cholesterol out of your bloodstream to make new ones. And sardines are one of the few whole foods packed with both omega-3s and vitamin D, a combo that helps turn down the inflammatory signals your joints send out when they're overworked. Everyone's body responds a little differently, so pay attention to what actually changes for you.
